newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Fotex leads Budapest bourse rebound.
newsitem.headline: Fotex leads Budapest bourse rebound.

text.p: Retailer Fotex led a modest rebound on the Budapest bourse on Monday, traders said, adding the market has calmed after Friday's 140-point plunge.
On Monday the BUX index closed at 5,512.11 points, up 49.23. BUX futures rose for all maturities, by between 10 and 62.50 points. March BUX closed at 5,577.5 points, up 42.50.
"After Friday's plunge the market has calmed and many stocks corrected upwards," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities.
Last Friday most traders attributed the sharp fall of the index to the effect of panic withdrawals of cash by customers of Postabank, Hungary's second largest commercial bank.
Traders said the market was mostly influenced by local factors today rather than by trend on major foreign markets.
On Monday Fotex shares caught traders unguarded by a nearly 16 percent or 22 forint rise to close at 160.
"Fotex's surge was a huge surprise for me," Nagy said.
Earlier today other traders said they could not give any explanation for the sudden rally in Fotex's share saying they were unaware of any new developments in the group.
However, in a statement in the official bourse gazette, Fotex said today that subscription period for the second tranche of Fotex's Gemini convertible bonds opened on March 1.

The day's gainers included tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt which closed more than two percent higher at 8,500 forints, although below the day's peak of 8,700 forints, after it announced that it had acquired a 79.3 percent stake in Croatia's Inker ceramics factory.
But traders said Zalakeramia's rise resulted from the market's sentiment rather than from the news itself.

"I think the market is coming back from Friday's bottom," one trader said earlier today. "The market knew that Zalakeramia wanted to make acquisitions and now that a deal has actually been made the announcement did not trigger any price rallies."
Traders said they expected sideways price movements remain the underlying trend until details of the next phase of privatisation in oil company MOL come through.
"Everybody awaits the MOL share issue," Nagy said.
